'''Sylvester James Gates Jr.''' (born December 15, 1950), known as '''S. James Gates Jr.''' or '''Jim Gates''', is an American [[theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] who works on [[supersymmetry]], [[supergravity]], and [[superstring theory]]. He is currently the Toll Professor of Physics at the University of Maryland. He also holds the Clark Leadership Chair in Science with the physics department at the [[University of Maryland College of Computer, Mathematical, and Natural Sciences]]. He is also affiliated with the University of Maryland's School of Public Policy. He previously was the Brown University Theoretical Physics Center Director and the Ford Foundation Professor of Physics. He served on former president [[Barack Obama]]'s [[Council of Advisors on Science and Technology]].<ref>{{cite web |title=UMD PCAST announcement |publisher=[[University of Maryland]] |url=http://www.newsdesk.umd.edu/scitech/print.cfm?articleID=1882 |access-date=April 30, 2009 |archive-date=February 28, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140228014045/http://www.newsdesk.umd.edu/scitech/print.cfm?articleID=1882 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Early life and education==

Gates, the oldest of four siblings, was born in [[Tampa, Florida]], the son of Sylvester James Gates Sr., a career [[United States Army|U.S. Army]] man, and Charlie Engels Gates. His mother died at age 44 of breast cancer when he was 11. Gates, Sr. raised his children while serving full-time in the U.S. Army and retired as a [[Sergeant Major of the Army|sergeant major]] after 27 years of service — one of the first African Americans to earn this position. Gates, Sr., later worked in public education and as a union organizer.<ref>{{Cite web |title=S. James Gates, Jr. Endows New Summer Research Award - UMD Physics |url=https://umdphysics.umd.edu/about-us/news/department-news/1766-donations.html |access-date=2023-02-01 |website=umdphysics.umd.edu}}</ref>

Both of Gates' parents were extraordinarily committed to their children's educations, though neither had the opportunity to go to college. Gates, Sr. never finished high school, as he enlisted in the U.S Army at the age of seventeen. He later earned a [[General Educational Development|G.E.D]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://umdphysics.umd.edu/about-us/news/department-news/1766-donations.html | title=S. James Gates, Jr. Endows New Summer Research Award - UMD Physics }}</ref> The family moved many times while Gates was growing up, but, in January 1963, settled in [[Orlando, Florida]], where Gates Jr. attended [[Jones High School (Orlando, Florida)|Jones High School]]—his first experience in a [[Racial segregation in the United States|segregated]] African-American school. Comparing his own school's quality to neighboring white schools, "I understood pretty quickly that the cards were really stacked against us."<ref>Henry Aller, "Sylvester James Gates (1950-)," Black Past, at https://www.blackpast.org/african-american-history/gates-sylvester-james-1950/ , retrieved 2019/09/28.</ref> Nevertheless, an 11th grade course in physics established Gates' career interest in physics, especially its mathematical side. At his father's urging, he applied for admission to [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]].

Gates received two [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] degrees from MIT in mathematics and physics (1973), as well as his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] (1977). For his undergraduate thesis he wrote ''On the Feasibility of Generating Electricity with a Rijke Tube''.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://umdphysics.umd.edu/people/faculty/current/item/167-gatess.html | title=Gates, Sylvester - UMD Physics }}</ref> His doctoral thesis, under the mentorship of [[James Edward Young|James E. Young]], was the first at MIT on [[supersymmetry]]. With [[Marcus Grisaru|M. T. Grisaru]], [[Martin Rocek|M. Rocek]] and [[Warren Siegel|W. Siegel]], Gates coauthored ''Superspace, or One thousand and one lessons in supersymmetry'' (1984), the first comprehensive book on supersymmetry.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gates |first1=S. James |author-link1=Sylvester James Gates |last2=Grisaru |first2=M. T. |last3=Rocek |first3=M. |last4=Siegel |first4=W. |date=1983 |title=Superspace |publisher=[[American Institute of Physics]] |url=https://arxiv.org/find/hep-th/1/AND+au:+gates+ti:+lesson/0/1/0/all/0/1 }}</ref>

== Career ==
Gates has taught every year since 1972.<ref name=":0" /> After his graduation from MIT in 1977, Gates accepted a Junior Fellowship at Harvard, the first Black scientist to be appointed a Junior Fellow.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Physics |first=American Institute of |date=2022-02-17 |title=Sylvester James Gates, Jr. |url=https://www.aip.org/history-programs/niels-bohr-library/oral-histories/46941 |access-date=2025-02-24 |website=www.aip.org |language=en}}</ref> He remained at Harvard until 1980, when he accepted a postdoctoral research appointment at [[California Institute of Technology|CalTech]], which lasted until 1982. He was the first Black postdoctoral researcher to be appointed in CalTech's Division of Physics, Mathematics, and Astronomy at Caltech.<ref name=":0" /> In 1982, he returned to MIT as an assistant professor of physics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=S. James Gates, Jr. at Interphase, 1975 {{!}} MIT Black History |url=https://www.blackhistory.mit.edu/archive/s-james-gates-jr-interphase-1975 |access-date=2025-02-24 |website=www.blackhistory.mit.edu |language=en}}</ref> In 1984, he gained an associate professor position at the University of Maryland (UMD) physics department. Four years later, he became a full professor of physics at UMD, a position he held until 2017, becoming the first African American to have an endowed position in physics at a major American research university.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Suplee |first=Anne |title=Gates, Sylvester - UMD Physics |url=https://umdphysics.umd.edu/people/faculty/current/item/167-gatess.html |access-date=2022-10-07 |website=umdphysics.umd.edu |language=en-us}}</ref>

In 1990, Gates was invited to serve as the chair of an external committee to evaluate the physics department at [[Howard University]]. After he submitted the committee's report to the dean, he was asked to join Howard as the chair of the physics department. He accepted and took a leave of absence from UMD from 1991-1993 to serve as chair of the department at Howard.<ref name=":0" /> While there, he led the creation of a new NASA-funded research center, called the Center for the Study of Terrestrial and Extraterrestrial Atmospheres (CSTEA), of which he served as the first director.<ref name=":0" />

Gates returned to UMD in 1993 and remained there until his retirement in 2017. Just prior to that, he spent a year at Dartmouth as the Roth Distinguished Scholar from 2015-2016.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Biography – Sylvester James Gates, Jr. |url=https://sites.brown.edu/sjgates/bio/ |access-date=2025-02-24 |website=sites.brown.edu |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2017, he retired from UMD as an emeritus professor and joined Brown University as the Director of the Brown Theoretical Physics Center, the Ford Foundation Professor of Physics, an Affiliate Mathematics Professor, and a Faculty Fellow in the Watson Institute for International Studies & Public Affairs.<ref name=":1" /> In 2022 Gates rejoined the University of Maryland as the John S. Toll Professor of Physics, Clark Leadership Chair in Science in the department of physics and the school of public policy at the University of Maryland.<ref>{{cite web |last=Gates |first=Sylvester James |date=2022-10-07 |title=THE CURRICULUM VITAE OF SYLVESTER JAMES GATES, JR |url=https://umdphysics.umd.edu/images/CV/Gates_CV_July_1_2022.pdf |access-date=2022-10-07}}</ref> Gates is on the board of trustees of [[Society for Science & the Public]] and is active in scientific outreach.
[[File:Gates Lectures.jpg|alt=S. James Gates lectures from a chalkboard.|left|thumb|S. James Gates lectures from a chalkboard]]

Gates was a Martin Luther King Jr. Visiting Scholar at MIT (2010–11) and was a residential scholar at MIT's [[List of Massachusetts Institute of Technology undergraduate dormitories#Simmons Hall .28W79.29|Simmons Hall]]. He is pursuing ongoing research into string theory, supersymmetry, and supergravity. His current research focus is on [[Adinkra symbols (physics)|Adinkra symbols]], a graph-theoretic technique for studying supersymmetric representation theories.

In 2018, Gates was elected to the presidential line of the [[American Physical Society]]: he began serving as its vice president in 2019, served as president in 2021, and past president in 2022.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://news.brown.edu/articles/2018/08/gates|title=Gates elected to presidential line of the American Physical Society|access-date=August 22, 2018|language=en}}</ref> He is also a past president of the [[National Society of Black Physicists]] (NSBP).<ref name=":1" />

==Research==
Gates' research has played a foundational role in understanding twisted multiplets and their implications for nonlinear [[sigma model]]s, generalized complex geometry, and [[Duality (mathematics)|duality]] in [[Supersymmetry|supersymmetric theories]]. He has also authored more than 200 research papers<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sylvester James Gates, Jr. |url=https://www.societyforscience.org/people/sylvester-james-gates-jr/ |access-date=2025-09-24 |website=Society for Science |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Supersymmetric sigma models and twisted multiplets===
In the 1980s, Gates co-authored a series of papers that introduced the twisted chiral multiplet, an extension of conventional chiral superfields in two-dimensional [[Supersymmetry|supersymmetric]] [[Quantum field theory|field theories]]. Unlike standard chiral [[Supermultiplet|multiplets]], which are constrained by Kähler geometry, twisted [[Supermultiplet|multiplets]] allow for the formulation of [[sigma model]]s on more general [[hermitian manifold]]s with torsion. This work provided insights into the geometric structure of [[Supersymmetry|supersymmetric theories]] and extended the classification of [[sigma model]]s beyond the constraints established by Alvarez-Gaume and Freedman.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Friedan |first1=Daniel Harry |title=Nonlinear models in 2 + ε dimensions |journal=Annals of Physics |date=September 1985 |volume=163 |issue=2 |pages=318–419 |doi=10.1016/0003-4916(85)90384-7 |bibcode=1985AnPhy.163..318F |url=https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark:/67531/metadc841801/ }}</ref>

===Generalized geometry and extended supersymmetry===
Gates' research demonstrated that [[supersymmetry|supersymmetric]] [[sigma model]]s incorporating twisted [[Supermultiplet|multiplets]] naturally exhibit two commuting complex structures, forming an almost product structure on the target space. This structure closely aligns with Generalized Kähler Geometry, a framework later formalized in Generalized Complex Geometry by [[Nigel Hitchin]] and Marco Gualtieri.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/generalized+complex+geometry | title=Generalized complex geometry in nLab }}</ref> His work also explored how dimensional reduction of four-dimensional vector [[Supermultiplet|multiplets]] leads to the emergence of twisted chiral [[Supermultiplet|multiplets]] in two dimensions, highlighting deep connections between higher-dimensional supersymmetric theories and lower-dimensional field theories with torsion-preserving symmetries.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=James Gates |first1=S. |title=Superspace formulation of new non-linear sigma models |journal=Nuclear Physics B |date=June 1984 |volume=238 |issue=2 |pages=349–366 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(84)90456-5 |bibcode=1984NuPhB.238..349J }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gates |first1=S.J. |last2=Hull |first2=C.M. |last3=Roc̆ek |first3=M. |title=Twisted multiplets and new supersymmetric non-linear σ-models |journal=Nuclear Physics B |date=December 1984 |volume=248 |issue=1 |pages=157–186 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(84)90592-3 |bibcode=1984NuPhB.248..157G }}</ref>

===Duality, torsion, and applications in string theory===
A major theme in Gates' work is the role of [[Duality (mathematics)|duality]] transformations in [[Supersymmetry|supersymmetric theories]]. He showed that chiral and twisted chiral multiplets are dual to each other under certain conditions, a result that mirrors [[T-duality]] in [[string theory]], where B-field transformations relate [[sigma model]]s with and without torsion. His contributions have influenced research in [[Superstring theory|superstring]] [[Compactification (physics)|compactifications]], particularly in scenarios where non-Kähler geometries arise due to background fluxes.{{Citation needed|date=March 2025}}

== Bucket list ==
[[File:Gates Einstein poster.jpg|thumb|Gates seated with Einstein poster on wall behind him]]
Gates keeps a [[Kick the bucket|bucket list]] with the experimental discoveries that he would like to see happening before he dies.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2014-10-22 |title=A theorist's bucket list |url=https://physicsworld.com/a/a-theorists-bucket-list/ |access-date=2025-03-12 |website=Physics World |language=en-GB}}</ref> As of 2025, his list includes five items:<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnston |first=Hamish |date=2025-02-20 |title=Jim Gates updates his theorist's bucket list and surveys the damage being done to US science and society |url=https://physicsworld.com/a/jim-gates-updates-his-theorists-bucket-list-and-surveys-the-damage-being-done-to-us-science-and-society/ |access-date=2025-03-12 |website=Physics World |language=en-GB}}</ref>

# [[Search for the Higgs boson]] (confirmed in 2013)
# [[First observation of gravitational waves]] (confirmed in 2015)
# Evidence of [[superpartner]]s (not yet demonstrated)
# Evidence of string theory (not yet demonstrated)
# Classical models that demonstrate quantum behaviour (not yet demonstrated)

== Awards and recognition ==
Gates' work has earned him recognition by [[Mathematically Gifted & Black]] as a [[Black History Month]] 2017 Honoree.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sylvester James Gates Jr.|url=https://mathematicallygiftedandblack.com/honorees/sylvester-james-gates-jr/|website=Mathematically Gifted & Black}}</ref>

On February 1, 2013, Gates was a recipient of the [[National Medal of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://bigstory.ap.org/photo/barack-obama-sylvester-james-gates-0 |title=Barack Obama, Sylvester James Gates |access-date=July 27, 2013 |archive-date=March 20, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150320180439/http://bigstory.ap.org/photo/barack-obama-sylvester-james-gates-0 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Gates was elected to the [[American Philosophical Society]] in 2012,<ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Member History|url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=S.+James+Gates&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced|access-date=2021-03-19|website=search.amphilsoc.org}}</ref> and the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |title=S. James Gates |website=www.nasonline.org |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/s-james-gates-jr-y9vgvs/ |access-date=July 28, 2015}}</ref>

Gates was nominated by the [[United States Department of Energy|Department of Energy]] as one of the [[USA Science and Engineering Festival]]'s "Nifty Fifty" Speakers to present his work and career to middle- and high-school students in October 2010.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130416042446/http://www.usasciencefestival.org/schoolprograms/niftyfifty.html?pid=420&sid=529:Dr-Sylvester-James|title=Nifty Fifty}}, [[USA Science and Engineering Festival]]</ref>

On December 5, 2016, Gates spoke at the 2016 Quadrennial Physics Congress, the largest ever gathering of physics undergraduates.

In 1994, Gates received the [[Edward A. Bouchet]] Award from the [[American Physical Society]] "for his contributions to theoretical high-energy physics."<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Gates&first_nm=Sylvester&year=1994 |title=1994 Edward A. Bouchet Award Recipient}}</ref> In 2023 Gates was awarded an [[Honorary degree|honorary doctorate]] by the [[University of the Witwatersrand]] in recognition of his contributions to science and his inspiring leadership in the scientific communities in Africa.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-07-17 |title=2023 - Wits honours Gates - Wits University |url=https://www.wits.ac.za/news/latest-news/graduations/2023/wits-honours-gates.html |access-date=2023-07-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230717215755/https://www.wits.ac.za/news/latest-news/graduations/2023/wits-honours-gates.html |archive-date=July 17, 2023 }}</ref>

He was elected to the 2026 class of Fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_year.cgi|title=2026 Class of Fellows of the AMS|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=2025-11-08}}</ref>

==Media appearances==
Gates has been featured in [[TurboTax]] and Verizon commercials and has been featured extensively on ''[[Nova (American TV series)|NOVA]]'' PBS programs on physics, notably ''[[The Elegant Universe]]'' (2003). He completed a DVD series titled ''Superstring Theory: The DNA of Reality'' (2006) for [[The Teaching Company]] consisting of 24 half-hour lectures to make the complexities of unification theory comprehensible to laypeople.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sylvester James Gates Jr. lecture|work=News@Concordia|publisher=[[Concordia University (Quebec)|Concordia University]]|url=http://news.concordia.ca/faculties/007534.shtml|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061004161201/http://news.concordia.ca/faculties/007534.shtml|archive-date=October 4, 2006}}</ref>

During the 2008 [[World Science Festival]], Gates narrated a ballet "The Elegant Universe", where he gave a public presentation of the artistic forms connected to his scientific research.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Armitage |first1=Karole |author-link1=Karole Armitage |last2=Ligeti |first2=Lukas |author-link2=Lukas Ligeti |last3=Gates |first3=Jim |title=The Elegant Universe |publisher=[[New York Academy of Sciences]] |work=Science & the City Podcast |url=http://www.nyas.org/Publications/Media/PodcastDetail.aspx?cid=6e4f1267-19b8-4618-ab20-167b74c74efc |access-date=December 1, 2015}}</ref> Gates Appeared on the 2011 [[Isaac Asimov Memorial Debate]]: The Theory of Everything, hosted by [[Neil DeGrasse Tyson]].<ref>{{youTube|lYeN66CSQhg|2011 Isaac Asimov Memorial Debate: The Theory of Everything}}</ref> Gates also appeared in the BBC [[Horizon (BBC TV series)|Horizon]] documentary ''The Hunt for Higgs'' in 2012, and the NOVA documentary ''Big Bang Machine'' in 2015.
